description: Sam Cox — last apprentice of Gordon Ford and principal of Sam Cox Landscape — has spent nearly three decades shaping this 1.5-acre Wattle Glen bush garden into one of the finest examples of Australian naturalistic design in private hands. Directly adjacent to a Nillumbik council green wedge corridor, the garden moves through earth-shaped terrain and layered native planting to a winding watercourse that feeds a large basalt-lined pond — habitat for frogs, birds and other wildlife. A waterfall brings water movement into the living spaces on the other side of the house. Thirty indigenous species now span all five structural layers. The garden opened through Open Gardens Victoria in November 2023 and carries the highest ecological function score in the Ecological Registry.

soil_water.mulch_type: Arborist mulch — self-generating from garden prunings

habitat.planting_method: Australian naturalistic design by Sam Cox Landscape — earth shaping, considered basalt rockwork, and layered indigenous planting across five structural layers. Winding watercourse leads to a large basalt-lined pond; a separate waterfall brings water sound into the family living spaces. All layers now self-seeding and self-sustaining after nearly three decades of ecological management.

milestones.title: Corridor node confirmed — Nillumbik green wedge

activity_log.title: Open Gardens Victoria — public garden opening
activity_log.notes: Garden opened to the public through Open Gardens Victoria, November 2023. Recognised as an exemplar of Australian naturalistic landscape design in private hands. Sam Cox Landscape's own home garden profiled alongside the studio's broader project work.

activity_log.title: G&S ecological assessment — corridor node confirmed
activity_log.notes: Full site assessment by Gardener & Son. Garden assessed across all five scoring pillars. 30 indigenous species confirmed across five structural layers. Superb Fairywren nesting pair and possum nest box occupancy documented. Rainwater collection, seasonal moisture basin, and swale all functioning. Garden confirmed as a corridor node and founding garden of the Nillumbik cluster. Score: 86/100.

activity_log.title: Breeding Superb Fairywren confirmed
activity_log.notes: Breeding pair of Superb Fairywren documented nesting in established Leptospermum continentale hedge. First confirmed nesting record for this garden. Possum nest box occupancy also confirmed on the same visit.

activity_log.title: Water feature and swale installed
activity_log.notes: Seasonal moisture basin and garden swale installed to close the water cycle. Combined with existing 5,000L rainwater tank, the garden now manages all rainfall on-site.

activity_log.title: 30th indigenous species established
activity_log.notes: Pratia puberula (Hairy Pratia) planted as the 30th locally indigenous species, completing the groundcover layer. All five structural layers now occupied by indigenous species. Indigenous species dominant across the planting. Garden has been actively managed since 1997.

notes: Highest-scoring garden in the Ecological Registry. Designer is Sam Cox (samcoxlandscape.com) — this is his own home garden. 1.5 acres (6,070m²). Field notes are the only outstanding evidence gap. Connectivity will rise significantly as neighbouring Nillumbik gardens register.
